This '''species''' was a [[Sentience|sentient]] [[species]] that existed in [[the galaxy]]. [[Loatha Sommover]] was a member of this species.<ref name="TLJ" />

==Biology and appearance==
This large [[species]] was distinguished by elongated, caterpillar-like bodies, which featured various rolls, creases, and a thick, segmented tail. They possessed ten stubby limbs, with [[Color|orang]] and brown mottled skin. Their locomotion could be assisted via [[repulsorlift]] platforms.<ref name="TLJ" />

==Species in the galaxy==
In [[34 ABY]],<ref name="Date Note">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' places the events of [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']] in [[34 ABY]]. ''Star Wars'': Episode VIII ''The Last Jedi'' takes place immediately after the end of ''The Force Awakens''.</ref> a member of this species, [[Loatha Sommover]], was present in [[Canto Bight]] on the [[planet]] [[Cantonica]].<ref name="TLJ" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Loatha-Sommover-Concept.jpg|thumb|right|200px|King 12 by Ivan Manzella]]
The species made their onscreen debut in the [[2017]] film {{Film|VIII}}, directed by [[Rian Johnson]].<ref name="TLJ" /> They were originally designed by creature concept designer and sculptor [[Ivan Manzella]],<ref name="Manzella">{{WebCite|url=https://www.krop.com/ivanmanzella|text=Ivan Manzella - Creature & Character Designs|archivedate=20240604150100}}</ref> and were referred to by the production code "King 12."<ref name="art">''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Last Jedi]]''</ref> According to the Keeper of the Holocron, [[Leland Chee]], as of [[April 1]], [[2025]], this species still did not have a name within the official [[Holocron continuity database]].<ref name="Unnamed Aliens">{{WookDiscord|discordname=.holocronkeeper|name=Leland Chee|date=2025-04-01|messagelink=https://discord.com/channels/397848917036761090/492457166771322881/1356720840036847656|archivefile=File:Holocron-Keeper-Unnamed-Species-TLJ.png}}</ref>
